facts.claim: TXN reported Q2 2026 revenue of $5.463B, up 23% year over year, with broad growth led by industrial, data center and automotive; first-half 2026 revenue was $10.29B, up 21% year over year.

Q2 2026 gross margin rose to 59.8% from 57.4% in the first half comparison, while higher manufacturing costs from planned capacity expansions remained an offset; TXN stated higher factory loadings spread fixed costs over more output and generally improve margins.

TXN expected $2B-$3B of 2026 capital expenditures, down from the elevated build cycle, and disclosed up to $1.6B of CHIPS direct funding for three large-scale 300mm fabs, of which $630M had been received by Q2 2026.

The U.S. Department of Commerce described TXN's Sherman and Lehi projects as expanding U.S. current-generation and mature-node semiconductor capacity and estimated more than 2,000 manufacturing jobs plus thousands of construction jobs over time.

risks.risk: Capacity economics remain utilization-sensitive: the filing states higher factory loadings improve margins, implying a demand relapse can leave fixed manufacturing costs underabsorbed.
Planned capacity expansion still increased manufacturing costs in first-half 2026 even as revenue and gross margin improved.

unknowns: Current market valuation and peer-relative valuation are not established by these sources and remain Alpha underwriting work.
Incremental return on each new 300mm fab is not separately quantified in these sources.
recommendation: Reuse the independent SEC and U.S. Department of Commerce origins to construct source-addressed underwriting factor, risk and confidence evidence. Scout does not assign numeric underwriting or canonical scores.
